title: The Recycling Experiment
story:
The eco club wanted to know which waste broke down fastest in the school garden. They chose four safe items: a lettuce leaf, a piece of paper, a plastic spoon, and a cotton square. Each item went into a mesh bag with a wooden label. The pupils buried the bags ten centimetres deep in the same damp corner, where the soil and the shade were almost the same.

They started on the first of October. Every Friday they lifted the bags, looked, and buried them again. In week one the lettuce was already brown and soft. The paper was wrinkled but whole. The cloth and the spoon looked new.

By week four the lettuce was gone, and only a wet stain remained. The paper had torn into grey pieces. The cotton was thinner, with a small hole at one edge. The plastic spoon was still smooth and the same shape. Their teacher, Ruth, said plastic can stay in soil for a very long time. That is why it should go to a recycling bin, not into the ground.

The club's report gave three ideas. Food scraps could go into the compost. Paper and cotton changed slowly. Plastic did not belong in the soil. They showed the photos at assembly, and clearer signs were promised for the bins. The test made the word biodegradable easier to trust, because the pupils had watched the changes themselves.

quiz.question: In this story, what does biodegradable mean?
options: Safe to burn in a classroom
quiz.explanation: The pupils trust the word after watching some items change and break down in the soil.
quiz.supportingSentence: The test made the word biodegradable easier to trust, because the pupils had watched the changes themselves.

quiz.question: Where should the plastic spoon go, according to Ruth?
quiz.explanation: Ruth says plastic stays in soil a long time, so it should go to a recycling bin.
quiz.supportingSentence: That is why it should go to a recycling bin, not into the ground.

quiz.question: Why did the club most likely choose one corner for every bag?
options: They wanted the soil and shade to be as equal as possible
That corner was the only place with labels
The spoon needed more sun than the paper
Ruth asked them to test unsafe chemicals
quiz.correctAnswer: They wanted the soil and shade to be as equal as possible
quiz.explanation: All the bags share one damp corner where the soil and shade are almost the same, so the test is fair.
